clue.text: Where climber may be trained in mountain, terrifying figure returning

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembled word is read backwards, coming back the way it went
in places the monster inside the mountain word

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
an ogre is a frightening giant of fairy tales

explanation.surface: A mountaineer meets something monstrous on the peak and turns back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant; 'returning' turns the whole assembly round.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden arch or framework over which climbing plants such as roses are grown and tied in.

clue.text: Crock shoots lots of elephants, say

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game, so pots means shoots
a large group of elephants is called a herd

explanation.surface: A hunter's crockery-like ineptitude, or someone bagging many elephants on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crock' suggests a useless person or old car; here it is a fragment of broken earthenware.
explanation.definitionFit: A crock can be a broken piece of pottery, which is exactly what this archaeological term names.

clue.text: Make unwelcome appearance hurriedly, as gatecrashing

indicators.note: crashing, the tail of one printed word, suggests a smash that throws these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rushes in uninvited at a party, gatecrashing in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: One printed word does two jobs: GATE, the front of 'gatecrashing', joins HURRIEDLY and AS as fodder, and its tail 'crashing' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a problem or unpleasant thing emerging or showing itself again, unwanted.

clue.text: Shop, perhaps as a means to express emotions

definitions.meaning: a retail store selling a maker's goods, e.g. a factory shop
a release or vent for feelings, such as sport for aggression

explanation.surface: Retail therapy as a way of letting off steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of a way out: a sales point for goods and a vent for feelings.

clue.text: A person helping you over your loss of interest

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first pieces above the next

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An assistant helps you get over losing interest in things.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, a lack of enthusiasm or concern for anything.

clue.text: Relaxed, prepared for another shot

definitions.meaning: posed again for the camera, read as RE- plus posed

explanation.surface: A model who has taken a rest is ready for the next photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is resting at ease; the other splits into RE (again) plus posed for a photograph.

clue.text: Extremely rare, expensive clothes in industrial plant

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters of the next word

parts.note: finery is elaborate, showy dress

explanation.surface: Factory workers dressed in unusually costly outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is a factory where crude materials like oil or sugar are purified.

clue.text: Turn somersault before degree is taken

indicators.note: a somersault turns things head over heels, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a flip is a turn, as in a gymnastic flip
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A gymnast performs a somersault before being awarded a qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilfered means stolen in small amounts, so it substitutes for taken as in purloined.

clue.text: Slyly peeking at bear browsing

parts.note: to shoulder a load is to bear it
surfing the web means browsing it

explanation.surface: Someone sneakily watching a grizzly that is grazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' and 'browsing' suggest an animal feeding; one is a verb for carrying, the other web activity.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes spying on someone's screen or keypad over their shoulder to steal information.

clue.text: Doctrine is compromising freedom to act

indicators.note: compromising suggests something weakened or altered, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A rigid creed undermines people's liberty to choose for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Discretion is the latitude to decide for oneself what should be done in a situation.

clue.text: Distinctive character of bird artist captured

indicators.note: captured means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter has caught the special look of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or feature of personality.

clue.text: Periodically, after Ge … like this

definitions.meaning: in the periodic table arsenic, symbol As, comes right after germanium, symbol Ge
a phrase that introduces what comes next, in the way set out below

explanation.surface: A sentence that trails off after an abbreviation, as if a list is about to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' points to the periodic table, where As follows Ge.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to introduce a list or quotation, meaning in the manner described next.

clue.text: Senior administrator's weakness, to risk register being rejected

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing
to chance something is to risk it

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a roll is a register of names

explanation.surface: A university chief's failing is gambling away the official record.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities this officer is the actual working head, the chancellor being largely ceremonial.

clue.text: After a false start, eat out without interruption

indicators.note: after puts the eating-out piece behind the earlier ones
false says the word start is not genuine, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to etch is to eat away a surface, as acid does

explanation.surface: After a bad beginning to the day, someone decides to dine at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' rearranges only the word 'start', giving TASTR; 'After' puts the eating-out piece at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in one continuous go, without a break, as in working for hours on end.

clue.text: Job to which poor performers are taken

definitions.meaning: a piece of work to be done

definitions.text: to which poor performers are taken
definitions.meaning: to be taken to ... is to be scolded for failing

explanation.surface: A post where underachievers get sent.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is an assigned piece of work, and the idiom 'taken to task' means rebuked.

clue.text: Taking minimum time in celebration of French produce?

indicators.note: of tells us what the festival celebrates, so the cheese comes first

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese
a fest is a festival or celebration

explanation.surface: A festival of French cheese that doesn't last long.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief means short, so the superlative describes whatever is the shortest in duration.

clue.text: Satellite phone is shut

parts.note: to call someone is to phone them
a door pushed to is shut

explanation.surface: A satellite phone that has been switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite phone' looks like one item; 'Satellite' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of Jupiter's large moons, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Knight risked capturing Stuart queen

indicators.note: capturing means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: bet means gambled, risked
Anne was the last Stuart monarch, with R for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A knight gambles on seizing a royal from the House of Stuart.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Anne (1702-14) was the last Stuart monarch; R is Regina, Latin for queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A banneret was a medieval knight entitled to lead men under his own banner.

clue.text: Relinquish, for example, being open to one worry constantly

indicators.note: being open to lets the other pieces in, so they go inside

parts.note: say means for example
I is the Roman numeral one
to gnaw is to fret persistently

explanation.surface: Someone giving something up because they are prone to constant anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign away is to give up a right or property formally by signature.

clue.text: Respecting footballers leaving new house

indicators.note: leaving means these letters go out of the club's name

parts.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club
a villa is a house

explanation.surface: Players departing from a newly built home.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English Premier League football club from Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean concerning or with regard to, as in a question about something.

clue.text: Joke the nervous get

definitions.meaning: a tease or prank meant to provoke someone
anxious people are said to get the ...

explanation.surface: A jest that frightened people receive.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom: a prank is a wind-up, and frightened people 'get the wind up'.

clue.text: Fighting disrupts work meeting in cave

indicators.note: disrupts means one word breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for communal work, as a sewing bee
war means fighting

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out at a meeting held in a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' looks like a hollow in rock; it is Latin for 'look out!', once schoolboy slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Cave is the Latin imperative of be wary, used as a schoolboy warning cry.

clue.text: Corps' senior general last to deploy bombs

definitions.note: possessive, with the 's read as is linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: bombs suggests explosion, sending these letters flying into a new order
last to points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An army general is the final one to deploy the bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to' takes Y from 'deploy', which joins the fodder before 'bombs' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the British Army corps of military engineers, nicknamed the Sappers.

clue.text: See 1
Loved pace: certain to get an innings

indicators.note: getting an innings means going in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to tread is to pace
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A cricketer's speed means they will definitely get to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a cricket batting turn; the clue borrows it for 'go in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is cherished and held dear.

clue.text: Having a rest, keeping very still with us

indicators.note: keeping means holding a letter inside

parts.note: a lie is a rest, as a lie-in

explanation.surface: Taking a break while staying perfectly still in our company.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still with us has not died, so is living.

clue.text: Retreat being awful to contemplate, finally advancing a position

indicators.note: the final letter moves on one place in the alphabet

parts.note: hideous means horrible to look at

explanation.surface: A terrible military withdrawal finally becomes a forward move.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of HIDEOUS moves one step along the alphabet to T.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a hiding place, a refuge to which one can retreat.

clue.text: Promised place, commonly equivocated

indicators.note: commonly suggests the dropped H of everyday Cockney speech

parts.note: to hedge is to avoid committing oneself

explanation.surface: A location where people typically avoided giving straight answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' drops the H, as in Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledged means gave one's word, made a solemn undertaking.
